2

Details

PSTAR ranges: 6.0 µm of Cu after the Li (872 keV), 8.7 µm with no Li at 1.15 MeV; ×1.12 + 1 µm for straggling, thickness error and roughness gives 10.7 µm, design 12 µm. Cu reaches ≥ 3 mm beyond the Li so no proton meets Li-on-Al or bare Al at full energy. Bare Al outside r 8 mm even with a 1 % halo makes 0.4 % of the γ₀ in ²⁷Al(p,γ). CU_LINER.md §1–4.

How it is built: one vacuum system, the source on the axis

the open base faces the source 150–400 mm away; aperture plates decide where each film ends

1 · Shell. Machine or spin the Al ogive, 0.35–0.4 mm, with a thick collar at the base for the joint (63 mm behind the tip, out of the arms' view).

2 · Cu. Ar-ion etch the inside, then sputter or evaporate 12–16 µm of Cu through a Ø12 mm aperture: it lands to r ≈ 10 mm. 1–2 h at 0.1–0.3 µm/min.

3 · Li. Without breaking vacuum (or under Ar), evaporate 20 µm of Li through a Ø4 mm aperture: it lands to r ≈ 4 mm, inside the Cu. A witness coupon records both thicknesses.

4 · On the line. Clamp the collar on an O-ring flange, adapter to DN40, He leak test. Minutes of PIGE at 1.10 MeV: no Al lines, 478 keV present.

3

Details

Schematic: the chamber, sources and masks show the geometry, not a real station. Aperture radii are for a point source on the axis 150 mm upstream of the tip, plate 78 mm in front of the source (Cu Ø11.9 mm, Li Ø4.3 mm); a real magnetron gives a penumbra of a few mm, which is why the Cu edge sits 6 mm beyond the Li edge. Plating instead (any shop): double zincate, Cu strike, acid Cu 15–20 µm with an anode wire on the axis, bake 150 °C; the Li still goes on from the axis. CU_LINER.md §8. The interactive version (rotate, step through) is on the target page.

Why lay both films from the axis

a line-of-sight coat lands ∝ cos(incidence), the same factor by which the beam's path through it grows

plated, uniform 12 µm: along the beam

from the axis: along the beam

from the axis: along the normal

On the 65° flank a film of fixed normal thickness is ×2.4 longer along the beam. For the Cu that is only wasted metal; for the Li it is a problem: the protons leave it below 441 keV and the 17.64 MeV line grows.

17.64 MeV share of the γ₀

Li film1.10 MeV1.03 MeV
same thickness along the normal29.3%70.7%
laid from the axis, r ≤ 40.9%1.4%

From the axis both films come out constant along the beam: 12–14 µm of Cu to r 8 mm, ~20 µm of Li everywhere. 1.03 MeV then costs only ~15 % against 1.10.

The price is Cu K x-rays (8 keV) from where the beam stops. Al absorbs them hard: each 0.1 mm divides what reaches the Micromegas by ~3.7. Hence 0.4 mm: 2.5 % occupancy per arm per µA, so up to ~4 µA.

Ti instead of Cu (15 µm) makes no x-ray that escapes and gives σ68 9.8°, but takes up hydrogen.

At full current your Cu ogive is not slow (no x-rays); the Al one wins on what matters for a claim: resolution, ×6 less EPC, ×2.8 fewer trigger legs.

Details

geant_reach.csv / geant_acceptance.csv; occupancies from the Geant4 L12 x-ray libraries × the Geant4 TestEm5 PIXE yields (Cu K as estimated, Mo K ×2 the earlier estimate). The floating-shape fit, which penalises poor resolution far more, has not been run on L11/L12 yet. Single-arm legs per µA into DREAM: 590 against 1630. CU_LINER.md §6–7.

Your view?

What we would like to know

1 · The beam spot at the target, σ and halo: it sets the Cu and mask radii (we assume σ 2 mm).

2 · Can the thin-film lab ion-etch, then sputter or evaporate ~15 µm of Cu inside the ogive from the axis, and Li through a mask, ideally without breaking vacuum?

3 · Can the workshop make the shell in Al 6061-T6 at 0.35–0.4 mm with a collar (not 0.2 mm)?

4 · What current do you expect? At ≤ 1 µA the x-rays never matter.

5 · Would Ti (15 µm) be as easy as Cu?
